problems.title: Integer and fractional parts
problems.question: How many real x satisfy floor(x)={x}+199?
problems.idea: Use the formulas below to reduce the problem to simpler quantities.
formulas: Write x=n+t, n integer, 0≤t<1.
steps: The equation is n=199+t. The only integer in [199,200) is199.
Thus t=0 and x=199 is the unique solution.

problems.title: A point off the unit circle
problems.question: Which listed point is not on the unit circle?
problems.idea: Use the formulas below to reduce the problem to simpler quantities.
formulas: A point (u,v) is on the unit circle exactly when u²+v²=1.
steps: The pairs involving complementary sines and cosines satisfy this identity.
For (cos160°,sin70°), cos160°=−cos20° and sin70°=cos20°, so the squared sum is 2cos²20°>1.

problems.title: Period of an absolute sine
problems.question: Find the least positive period of 3|sin(2x+1)|−9.
problems.idea: Use the formulas below to reduce the problem to simpler quantities.
formulas: |sin u| has least positive period π.
steps: The argument changes by 2T, so require 2T=π.
Multiplication and vertical shifting preserve the period.

problems.title: Distance from an elevated point to a side
problems.question: AB=10,AC=17,BC=21. AK=15 is perpendicular to the triangle’s plane. Find distance from K to BC.
problems.idea: Use the formulas below to reduce the problem to simpler quantities.
formulas: Heron: Δ=√[s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c)]; distance²=AK²+(altitude from A to BC)².
steps: Distance=√(15²+8²).

problems.title: A perpendicular and an oblique segment
problems.question: AB is parallel to a plane, BD=10 is perpendicular to it, and AC=20 meets the plane and is perpendicular to AB. AB=10√6. Find CD.
problems.idea: Use the formulas below to reduce the problem to simpler quantities.
formulas: A and B have the same height10; the projection of AC has length √(20²−10²)=10√3.
steps: AB is perpendicular to that projection because AB lies parallel to the plane and AB⊥AC.
CD is the hypotenuse of a planar right triangle with legs 10√6 and 10√3.

problems.title: Count functions with neither parity
problems.question: Among the five printed functions, how many are neither even nor odd?
problems.idea: Use the formulas below to reduce the problem to simpler quantities.
formulas: Even functions satisfy f(−x)=f(x); odd functions satisfy f(−x)=−f(x), on symmetric domains.
steps: (1−cosx)/(1+cosx) and both copies of 1−2sin²x+cosx are even.
(1−cos²x)/x⁵ is odd.
cosx+1/tanx is a sum of a nonzero even part and a nonzero odd part, so it has neither parity.

problems.title: Factor a difference of trigonometric squares
problems.question: Simplify tan²α−sin²α.
problems.idea: Use the formulas below to reduce the problem to simpler quantities.
formulas: tan²α−sin²α=sin²α(1/cos²α−1).
steps: The bracket is (1−cos²α)/cos²α=tan²α.

problems.title: Order sine, tangent and cosine
problems.question: Order a=tan27°,b=sin27°,c=cos27° increasingly.
problems.idea: Use the formulas below to reduce the problem to simpler quantities.
formulas: tanθ=sinθ/cosθ; for 0<θ<45°, sinθ<cosθ.
steps: Since cos27°<1, tan27°>sin27°.
Also tan27°<cos27° because sin27°<cos²27°; for example sin27°<1/2 while cos²27°>1/2.

problems.title: A line, its projection, and a planar line
problems.question: A line makes angle α with a plane and β with a line in that plane. Its projection makes angle γ with the planar line. Find the relation.
problems.idea: Use the formulas below to reduce the problem to simpler quantities.
formulas: The projection length of a unit line vector into the plane is cosα.
steps: Its component along the planar line is therefore cosα cosγ.
That same component is cosβ.

problems.title: A point equally distant from three triangle sides
problems.question: A point off the plane is distance3 from every side of a 5-12-13 triangle. Find its distance to the plane.
problems.idea: Use the formulas below to reduce the problem to simpler quantities.
formulas: For perpendicular height h and projection distance r from a side, 3²=h²+r².
steps: The projected point is a triangle incenter or excenter. The inradius is Δ/s=30/15=2. The exradii are3,10,15; none is less than3, as required for h>0.

problems.title: Reduce large trigonometric angles
problems.question: Evaluate sin960° cos495° tan(−840°)+cot240°.
problems.idea: Use the formulas below to reduce the problem to simpler quantities.
formulas: Use sine/cosine period360° and tangent/cotangent period180°.
steps: The factors are −√3/2,−√2/2,√3, and1/√3 respectively.
The value is 3√2/4+1/√3.

problems.title: Count integer roots of an inequality with sin6
problems.question: How many integers satisfy x²+2x+sin6<0, with angles in radians?
problems.idea: Use the formulas below to reduce the problem to simpler quantities.
formulas: −1<sin6<0, so (x+1)²<1−sin6 with 1<1−sin6<2.
steps: The integer x+1 can only be −1,0,1.
Thus x=−2,−1,0 all work.

problems.title: Quadrants visited by a quadratic
problems.question: Which quadrants contain points of y=(cos1)x²+(cos2)x+cos3? Angles are radians.
problems.idea: Use the formulas below to reduce the problem to simpler quantities.
formulas: cos1>0 and cos3<0.
steps: At x=0 the value is negative, so continuity gives negative y on both sides of zero: quadrants III and IV.
The positive leading coefficient makes y positive for sufficiently large positive and negative x: quadrants I and II.

problems.title: Distance to a short hexagon diagonal
problems.question: A point is √52 from every vertex and √43 from every side of a regular hexagon. Find its distance to a short diagonal.
problems.idea: Use the formulas below to reduce the problem to simpler quantities.
formulas: Let height to its plane be h and hexagon side a. Circumradius=a and apothem=√3a/2.
steps: Subtract the squared distance equations: a²−3a²/4=52−43=9, giving a=6.
Then h²=52−36=16. The center’s distance to a short diagonal is a/2=3.
The spatial distance is √(16+9).

problems.title: Two perpendicular offsets on different faces
problems.question: A,B lie on the edge of a 60° dihedral angle, AB=1. AC=2 and BD=3 are perpendicular to the edge on different faces. Find CD.
problems.idea: Use the formulas below to reduce the problem to simpler quantities.
formulas: The transverse offset has squared length AC²+BD²−2AC·BD cos60°.
steps: Add the squared component along the edge: CD²=1+4+9−6=8.

problems.title: Maximize a sine-and-cosine expression
problems.question: Find max(2sin²α+5cosα+3).
problems.idea: Use the formulas below to reduce the problem to simpler quantities.
formulas: Set c=cosα∈[−1,1], giving 5+5c−2c².
steps: Its derivative is5−4c>0 throughout [−1,1], so it increases on that interval.
At c=1 the value is5+5−2.

problems.title: Minimum of a linear sine combination
problems.question: Find the minimum of (√3/2)sinα+(1/2)cosα.
problems.idea: Use the formulas below to reduce the problem to simpler quantities.
formulas: A sinα+B cosα has amplitude √(A²+B²).
steps: Here the amplitude is √(3/4+1/4)=1.
The combination equals sin(α+π/6), which attains −1.

problems.title: Integer values of a rational sine expression
problems.question: How many integer values can 3/(2sinα+3) take?
problems.idea: Use the formulas below to reduce the problem to simpler quantities.
formulas: −1≤sinα≤1 gives 1≤2sinα+3≤5.
steps: The range is [3/5,3], and every value in it is attained.
Its integers are1,2,3.

problems.title: A quadrilateral with an equidistant off-plane point
problems.question: An off-plane point is equally distant from all four vertices of a planar quadrilateral. Which listed quadrilateral is impossible?
problems.idea: Use the formulas below to reduce the problem to simpler quantities.
formulas: Its orthogonal projection is equally distant from all vertices, so the quadrilateral is cyclic.
steps: A cyclic parallelogram has opposite angles both equal and supplementary, hence every angle is90°.
Thus a cyclic rhombus must be a square. A nonsquare rhombus is impossible.
problems.answer: A rhombus that is not a square.

problems.title: Right triangles in perpendicular planes
problems.question: Right triangles ABP,ABQ lie in perpendicular planes with common hypotenuse AB. AP=AQ=15√2 and BP=BQ=20√2. Find PQ.
problems.idea: Use the formulas below to reduce the problem to simpler quantities.
formulas: Both right-angle vertices have the same projection onto AB; their distances to AB equal the right-triangle altitude.
steps: The two altitude segments lie perpendicular to each other, so PQ=√[2(12√2)²].

problems.title: Choose the sign of a square root
problems.question: Find sin(199°+α) if sin(109°+α)=b and 80°≤α≤150°.
problems.idea: Use the formulas below to reduce the problem to simpler quantities.
formulas: Let u=109°+α. Then sin(u+90°)=cosu.
steps: 189°≤u≤259°, wholly in the third quadrant, so cosu<0.
Using cos²u=1−b², take the negative root.

problems.title: Factor a mixed trigonometric equation
problems.question: Find sin²α if 12tanα+sinα=12+tanα sinα.
problems.idea: Use the formulas below to reduce the problem to simpler quantities.
formulas: Rearrange as (tanα−1)(12−sinα)=0.
steps: The factor12−sinα cannot vanish, since |sinα|≤1.
Thus tanα=1, and sin²α=tan²α/(1+tan²α).

problems.title: When a perpendicularity implication fails
problems.question: Objects X,Y,Z are lines or planes. The claim “X⊥Y and X⊥Z implies Y is parallel to or contained in Z” is false. Which listed types can they have?
problems.idea: Use the formulas below to reduce the problem to simpler quantities.
formulas: Two distinct lines perpendicular to one line need not be parallel to one another.
steps: Take X as the z-axis and Y,Z as the x- and y-axes: both are perpendicular to X but cross each other.
This realizes the listed choice line,line,line. The other listed mixed types give the claimed parallelism or containment.
problems.note: Three planes can also give a counterexample: X the xy-plane, Y the xz-plane, Z the yz-plane. That type is omitted, so the word necessarily is too strong unless the choice list defines the allowed types.

problems.title: Pairwise intersection lines of three planes
problems.question: Three distinct planes meet pairwise in three distinct lines. Which relation between two intersection lines is impossible?
problems.idea: Use the formulas below to reduce the problem to simpler quantities.
formulas: Any two of these lines lie in one of the original planes.
steps: For example the lines P₁∩P₂ and P₁∩P₃ both lie in P₁.
Coplanar lines may intersect or be parallel but cannot be skew.
